contractSource: Description: "Divide land into equal plots instantly. Calculate plot sizes, dimensions, and optimal layouts with road spacing support." On-page: result card "Plot Size (Each)", "Road Area" with the note "Road area deducted from total", "Usable Land", "Layout" (rows × cols) and "Plot Dimensions" (width × length). Land units offered: Square Feet, Square Meter, Decimal, Acre, Katha, Bigha, Hectare.
groundTruth: Equal division: each plot = usable land ÷ number of plots. Internal roads run between the rows and between the columns of the plot grid; where a horizontal and a vertical road cross, the overlap is one road-width square and must be counted once. Unit facts used: 1 decimal = 1/100 acre = 435.6 sq ft (1 acre = 43,560 sq ft by definition).

cases.note: Plain equal division with no road — the core promise.
cases.derivation: 4,356 sq ft split into 4 equal plots: 4,356 ÷ 4 = 1,089 sq ft each.

cases.note: The same division in decimal, the unit this page's audience uses.
cases.derivation: 10 decimal split into 4 equal plots: 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5 decimal each. Division is unit-independent when no other quantity is involved.

cases.note: A square lot divided into a 2 × 2 grid with a 10 ft road between the rows and the columns — a cross of two roads.
cases.derivation: Lot 66 ft × 66 ft = 4,356 sq ft. A 2 × 2 grid needs one road across (66 ft × 10 ft = 660 sq ft) and one road down (66 ft × 10 ft = 660 sq ft). They overlap in a 10 ft × 10 ft square (100 sq ft) that must be counted once: road area = 660 + 660 − 100 = 1,220 sq ft. Usable land = 4,356 − 1,220 = 3,136 sq ft; per plot = 3,136 ÷ 4 = 784 sq ft. Each plot is (66 − 10) ÷ 2 = 28 ft wide and 28 ft long; check 28 × 28 = 784.

cases.note: The identical lot entered as 10 decimal. The answer must be the same land, expressed in decimal — and never negative.
cases.derivation: 10 decimal × 435.6 sq ft = 4,356 sq ft, the same 66 ft × 66 ft lot as the previous case. From that case each plot is 784 sq ft; 784 ÷ 435.6 = 1.7998 ≈ 1.80 decimal. A negative plot size is impossible for any real division of land.

cases.note: A prime plot count: 7 equal rectangles can only be laid out as 1 × 7 or 7 × 1, so the dimensions must multiply back to the plot area.
cases.derivation: Lot 70 ft × 40 ft = 2,800 sq ft, no road, 7 plots: 2,800 ÷ 7 = 400 sq ft each. Seven equal rectangles filling the lot are either 7 across (70 ÷ 7 = 10 ft wide × 40 ft long) or 7 down (70 ft wide × 40 ÷ 7 = 5.71 ft long); both give 400 sq ft. Any other pair (e.g. from an 8-cell 2 × 4 grid) does not multiply to 400.

expect.what: plot dimensions must be 10 × 40 ft or 70 × 5.71 ft (7 equal plots)
